text: Why is `ArrayList.add` O(1) amortized rather than O(n)?
choices: Because the copy happens on a background thread and does not block the caller.
Because the JIT eliminates the capacity check once the loop is proven hot.
Doubling to capacity n copies n-1 elements in total across n additions — fewer than one copy per add on average.
Because the array is over-allocated at construction, so no copy is ever needed in practice.
explanation: The sum 1 + 2 + 4 + ... + n/2 = n - 1 is Chapter 17's promised sum of powers of two. The rare expensive operation is paid for by the many cheap ones. Growing by a constant 10 instead would copy about n²/20 elements, making `add` O(n) amortized and building a list quadratic — which is the difference between a good dynamic array and a catastrophic one.
